rename.to: joinedload support with many-to-many based on PG-specific array functions

body:
hi -

have you tried using selectinload?   joinedload for collections is mostly obsolete at this point.

hi there -

you have your priamryjoin and secondaryjoin backwards.   If I correct it, it works:

```
join_primary = authors_books_selectable.c.author_id == Author.id
join_secondary = Book.id == authors_books_selectable.c.book_id

Author._relationship_books_ = relationship(
    Book,
    secondary=authors_books_selectable,
    primaryjoin=join_primary,
    secondaryjoin=join_secondary,
    viewonly=True,
)

```
for m2m from Parent->Child,   primaryjoin is Parent->m2m, secondaryjoin is m2m->Child.

joinedload query is:
```

SELECT authors.id AS authors_id, authors.name AS authors_name, authors.books AS authors_books, books_1.id AS books_1_id, books_1.name AS books_1_name 
FROM authors LEFT OUTER JOIN ((SELECT unnest(authors.books) AS book_id, authors.id AS author_id 
FROM authors) AS anon_1 JOIN books AS books_1 ON books_1.id = anon_1.book_id) ON anon_1.author_id = anon_1.author_id 
WHERE authors.id = %(id_1)s
```

is that what you expect?
your "working" version is using the backwards relationship for the join!  so yes.   just need to set these correctly.

Ok, I've replaced the part with relationships with this:

```python
# first, this way
join_primary = Book.id == authors_books_selectable.c.book_id  # book_id is a label for unnested ids
join_secondary = authors_books_selectable.c.author_id == Author.id  # author_id label from selectable

Book._relationship_inverse_authors_ = relationship(
    Author,
    secondary=authors_books_selectable,
    primaryjoin=join_primary,
    secondaryjoin=join_secondary,
    viewonly=True,
)


# swap priamryjoin and secondaryjoin
join_primary = authors_books_selectable.c.author_id == Author.id
join_secondary = Book.id == authors_books_selectable.c.book_id

Author._relationship_books_ = relationship(
    Book,
    secondary=authors_books_selectable,
    primaryjoin=join_primary,
    secondaryjoin=join_secondary,
    viewonly=True,
)
```

And now the output is:

```
-----
getting one author and his books using joined load

Compiled query:
SELECT authors.id, authors.name, authors.books, books_1.id, books_1.name 
FROM authors LEFT OUTER JOIN ((SELECT unnest(authors.books) AS book_id, authors.id AS author_id 
FROM authors) AS anon_1 JOIN books AS books_1 ON books_1.id = anon_1.book_id) ON anon_1.author_id = anon_1.author_id 
WHERE authors.id = 2
.
author: Author(name='A2', books=[2, 3])
his books: [Book(name='First'), Book(name='Second'), Book(name='Third')]
---
getting one author and his books using contains_eager

Compiled query:
SELECT authors.id, authors.name, authors.books, books.id, books.name 
FROM books JOIN (SELECT unnest(authors.books) AS book_id, authors.id AS author_id 
FROM authors) AS anon_1 ON books.id = anon_1.book_id JOIN authors ON anon_1.author_id = authors.id 
WHERE authors.id = 2
.
author: Author(name='A2', books=[2, 3])
his books: [Book(name='Second'), Book(name='Third')]
```

The compiled query looks like yours, but the result that it produces is not what I'm waiting for. The `joinedload` result is

```python
# author:
Author(name='A2', books=[2, 3])
# his books (call to author._relationship_books_):
[Book(name='First'), Book(name='Second'), Book(name='Third')]
```

As you can see, here we get the books 1,2,3, but the model contains only 2,3

But sure, we got rid of the `ProgrammingError`

So, is there a way to do it with the `joinedload` properly (fetching only related ids)? I'm out of ideas :(

P.S. no, I haven't tried `selectinload`.

The main reason I'm trying to do it with `joinedload` because it's already used in some libs like [flask_rest_jsonapi](https://github.com/miLibris/flask-rest-jsonapi/blob/b44bc08b11213d49fadae873650d3555889052ec/flask_rest_jsonapi/data_layers/alchemy.py#L573)

the problem with the query is the join condition at the end is pulling in the primary Author table to be adapted to match the secondary table:

```
SELECT authors.id AS authors_id, authors.name AS authors_name, authors.books AS authors_books, books_1.id AS books_1_id, books_1.name AS books_1_name 
FROM authors LEFT OUTER JOIN ((SELECT unnest(authors_1.books) AS book_id, authors_1.id AS author_id 
FROM authors AS authors_1) AS anon_1 JOIN books AS books_1 ON books_1.id = anon_1.book_id) ON **anon_1.author_id = anon_1.author_id** 
WHERE authors.id = %(id_1)s

```

that last part should say "anon_1.author_id = authors.id".   I'm even trying to apply an alias to Author inside the secondary table but it is still doing that.   seems like a bug, but then the documentation seems to suggest this is a known limitation:

https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/13/orm/join_conditions.html#relationship-to-aliased-class: 

> when we seek to join from A to B, making use of any number of C, D, etc. in between, however there are also join conditions between A and B directly. In this case, the join from A to B may be difficult to express with just a complex primaryjoin condition, as the intermediary tables may need special handling, and it is also not expressible with a secondary object, **since the A->secondary->B pattern does not support any references between A and B directly**.

again, I am going to look at the code to see why it's doing that, but the fact that I documented something very similar might mean it's unavoidable.

it already seems awkward to have this be a load of three separate selectables when there is nothing between A and B.     In fact it looks like just a plain custom join condition should work here, but alas:

```
sqlalchemy.exc.NotSupportedError: (psycopg2.errors.FeatureNotSupported) set-returning functions are not allowed in JOIN conditions
LINE 2: ... LEFT OUTER JOIN books AS books_1 ON books_1.id = unnest(aut...

```

So PG is going to force us to use all this nesting, so the relationship to aliased class pattern should be used:

```
from sqlalchemy.orm import aliased, foreign

subq = select(
    [Author.id.label("author_id"), func.unnest(Author.books).label("book_id")]
).alias()

subq = (
    select([Book, subq.c.author_id])
    .select_from(subq.join(Book, subq.c.book_id == Book.id))
    .alias()
)

BForA = aliased(Book, subq)


Author._relationship_books_ = relationship(
    BForA,
    primaryjoin=foreign(subq.c.author_id) == Author.id,
    viewonly=True,
)

```

rename.from: joinedload support with many-to-many based on PG-specific array functions
rename.to: apply omission of "local" columns when applying aliasing to join conditions around a secondary

body:
**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **rel_1_3** branch:

**Exclude local columns when adapting secondary in a join condition** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1570
you can use relationship to secondary but the issue with "anon_1.id == anon_1.id" is fixed in the above gerrit and will be in 1.3.11.
err I mean you can use relationship to aliased class right now.

# :fire: 

Super nice!

And aliased works, thanks a lot!

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Exclude local columns when adapting secondary in a join condition** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1571
